operator_io_quirks: All declared types are plain TEXT/INTEGER/REAL/DATE; no mixed-case or spaced identifiers, no crash-fallback types, no bool/bit/year/time columns.
air_date and birthdate are declared DATE but stored as text 'YYYY-MM-DD'; ts_fuzzer shows 'Date|Number(int elements)' — the int-parse branch of the date dispatch must not fire on these strings.
birthdate has null_rate 0.554 and only 355 distinct of 800; Date sampler's element pool will be mostly NULLs (dropped by Base) plus ~5 sampled dates.
Episode.episode_id, Person.person_id, Keyword.episode_id, Award.episode_id/person_id, Credit.episode_id/person_id, Vote.episode_id are all TEXT ids ('tt…','nm…') — String fuzzer, not Number.
Vote has NO primary key (pk=[]); sample_fresh_primary_keys must be a no-op there and drop_unique_duplicates has no unique columns to act on.
Keyword and Credit have composite PKs (episode_id,keyword) / (episode_id,person_id); composite-PK members get max_l0=30 per spec 3.3.
Keyword.episode_id has only 3 distinct values over 33 rows; Credit.person_id 798 distinct over 2231 — FK fan-out is very uneven.
All FKs point to existing parents (Episode, Person); no dangling FKs, no self-references, no non-unique parents.
Episode.series and Award.series are constant 'Law and Order' (distinct=1); season distinct=1; year distinct=2 — String/Number samplers will see near-constant element pools.
Credit.credited stores 'true'/'false' as TEXT (not BOOL type) — String fuzzer, not Bool.
Episode.summary, episode_image, Person.name/birth_* are long free text; String fuzzer's 20-char default length range will produce much shorter values than originals.
Tables are tiny (24–2231 rows); choose_table_sizes' 30–2500 range will often exceed original sizes, so FK child tables may draw from small parent pools with heavy duplication.
operator_ts_expectations: Date fuzzer on air_date/birthdate: template inferred from first parsable element, likely '%Y-%m-%d'; fresh dates uniform over [min,max] of parsed elements (1998–2000 for air_date, ~1930–1990 for birthdate).

Number fuzzer on season/episode/number_in_series/stars/votes/year/award_id: full range [-10^scale,10^scale] with scale=0 → integers in [-1,1] perturbed by ±1/±2, so most values collapse to {-3..3} — implausible for episode numbers (182+) and votes (hundreds).

Number fuzzer on rating/height_meters/percent (REAL, scale=0): range [-1,1] with ±0.01/±0.02 perturbation — rating 7.9 and percent 17.7 become ~0.x, a strong FN source for range predicates like rating>8 or percent>20.
String fuzzer on episode_id/person_id: random 0–20 char strings over a-zA-Z 0-9() with 50% contamination — destroys the 'tt…'/'nm…' prefix pattern, so LIKE 'tt%' or substr predicates will miss.
String fuzzer on credited: element pool {'true','false'} plus random strings; equality predicates on credited='true' will often see random garbage instead.

String fuzzer on series/season-like constants: element pool has one value, so p-fresh draws still inject random strings — GROUP BY series will produce many spurious groups (FP for count-distinct queries).

FK fill draws from parent's FINAL filtered column with replacement: Keyword.episode_id (3 distinct) and Credit.person_id (798 distinct) will produce heavy duplicate FK values, so joins are dense — good for join FPs, bad for 'exactly one' predicates.
Vote has no PK, so no PK dedup; with 240 original rows and size up to 2500, Vote will have many duplicate (episode_id,stars,votes,percent) rows — COUNT(*) queries on Vote will over-count vs original.
Composite-PK dedup on Keyword/Credit keeps first occurrence only; with small parent pools the surviving rows may be far fewer than requested size, shrinking join cardinalities.

NULLs: TS does not enforce NOT NULL, but Base drops None elements and String/Number rarely emit None, so birthdate/birth_place/nickname null_rate ~0.55–0.96 will be ~0 in generated units — IS NULL predicates become trivially empty (FN).
Date fuzzer's leading-zero strip and month-name template don't apply here (no %d-%m-%Y, no leading-zero strings), so dates stay ISO — good for date comparisons.
Number fuzzer's list_max quirk (overwrite with full-range max) means even with element pool {182..186} the fresh draws still span [-1,1], so number_in_series loses its 182+ range.
